inputs.original_text: A Wisconsin jury convicted Harry Wait of election fraud and identity theft after he requested ballots for Assembly Speaker Robin Vos and Racine Mayor Cory Mason without their consent. Whatever the claimed motive, using other people’s identities to stage an election-security stunt can undermine trust—and give cover to those who want to make voting harder. The answer is safeguards that protect voters without piling new barriers onto people who already face obstacles to participating.
inputs.modified_text: A Wisconsin jury convicted Harry Wait of election fraud and identity theft after he requested ballots for Assembly Speaker Robin Vos and Racine Mayor Cory Mason without their consent. Turning other people’s identities into an election-security stunt is wrong—but the bigger danger is using incidents like this to justify making voting harder for everyone. The response should be targeted safeguards and accountability, not new barriers that fall hardest on people already facing obstacles to participation.
